source_text: siquidem a primordio rerum conditor harum cum ipsis pariter compertus est, ipsis ad hoc prolatis, ut deus cognosceretur. I nec enim si aliquanto posterior Moyses primus uidetur in templo litterarum suarum deum mundi dedicasse, idcirco a Pentateucho natales agnitionis supputabuntur, cum totus Moysei stilus notitiam creatoris non instituat, sed a primordio enarret, a paradiso et Adam, non ab Aegypto et Moyse recensendam, denique maior popularitas generis humani, ne nominis quidem Moysei compotes, nedum instrumenti, deum Moysei tamen norunt; etiam tantam idolatria dominationem obumbrante, seorsum tamen illum quasi proprio nomine deum') perhibent et \'deum deorum\' et \'si deus dederit\' et \'quod deo placet\' et \'deo commendo.\' uide, an nouerint quem omnia posse testantur. nec hoc ullis Moysei libris debent. ante anima quam prophetia. animae enim a primordio conscientia dei dos est; eadem nec alia et in Aegyptiis et in Syris et in Ponticis. [Iudaeorum enim deum dicunt animae deum.] noli, barbare haeretice, priorem Abraham constituere quam mundum. et si unius familiae deus fuisset creator, tamen posterior tuo non erat, etiam Ponticis ante eum notus. accipiat igitur ab antecessore formam, a certo incertus, a cognito incognitus: numquam deus latebit, numquam deus deerit, semper intellegetur, semper audietur, etiam uidebitur, quomodo uolet. habet deus testimonia: totum hoc quod sumus et in quo sumus. sic probatur et deus et unus, dum non ignoratur, alio adhuc probari laborante.
pass_a_gloss: For indeed from the beginning of things the founder of these things is understood together with them, these things having been brought forth so that God might be known. And not even if Moses seems to be somewhat later, the first in the temple of his writings to have dedicated the God of the world, for this reason the birthdays of recognition will be calculated from the Pentateuch, since the whole style of Moses does not establish the knowledge of the creator, but narrates from the beginning, from paradise and Adam, not from Egypt and Moses to be reckoned, finally the greater popularity of the human race, not even having Moses' name, nonetheless know the God of Moses; and even with such great idolatry dominating, nonetheless they proclaim him separately as if with his own name God, and 'God of gods' and 'if God gives' and 'what pleases God' and 'I commend to God.' See, whether they know the one whom they testify all things are able to do. Nor do they owe this to any books of Moses. Before prophecy, the soul. For the soul has been given the consciousness of God from the beginning; the same, and no other, also in the Egyptians and in the Syrians and in the Pontics. For they say the God of the soul is the God of the Jews. Do not, barbarous heretic, constitute Abraham as prior to the world. And if the creator had been the God of one family, nonetheless he was not later than you, even known to the Pontics before him. Therefore, let him receive form from the predecessor, from the certain the uncertain, from the known the unknown: never will God be hidden, never will God be lacking, always will he be understood, always will he be heard, and even seen, however he wishes. God has testimonies: the whole of this which we are and in which we are. Thus God is proven and one, while not being ignored, with another still laboring to prove.
pass_b_english: From the very beginning of creation, the Founder of all things has been known alongside the things He made, because He brought them into existence precisely so that God might be known (Genesis 1-3). And even if Moses appears somewhat later as the first to dedicate the God of the world in the temple of his writings, that does not mean we must date the birth of divine recognition from the Pentateuch. Moses' entire narrative does not establish knowledge of the Creator; it recounts that knowledge from the very start, from Paradise and Adam, not from Egypt and Moses. Indeed, the vast majority of the human race, who never even heard of Moses' name, let alone his books, still knew the God of Moses. Even under the blinding dominance of idolatry, they acknowledged Him separately, as it were, by His own proper name — calling Him 'God of gods,' saying 'if God gives,' 'what pleases God,' 'I commend to God.' Look at it: they bear witness to the One they confess can do all things, and they owe this knowledge to no book of Moses. The soul comes before prophecy. For the soul has carried the consciousness of God as a birthright from the beginning — the same consciousness, and no other, found also in Egyptians, Syrians, and Pontics (for they call the God of the soul the God of the Jews). So do not, you barbarous heretic, set Abraham before the world. Even if the Creator had been the God of a single family, He would still not be later than your god, since the Pontics knew Him before Abraham. Let your god therefore receive his definition from the predecessor: from the certain, the uncertain; from the known, the unknown. God will never be hidden, never be absent; He will always be understood, always be heard, and even seen, however He chooses. God has His witnesses: the whole of what we are and the world in which we live. Thus God is proven, and proven one, precisely because He is not ignored, while another still labors to prove his case.
